bug_semantics: Stored cross-site scripting in the CMS Asset Manager: a backend user who has cms.manage_assets can upload an SVG containing active script. The upload handler accepts svg by extension and writes the uploaded bytes unchanged into the selected theme's web-addressable assets directory; when another user opens or embeds that stored asset, the SVG script can execute in the site's origin. The first-party advisory rates exploitation as requiring a privileged backend account and user interaction.
flaw_origin: Commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 first created modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php. In that commit, line 56 put 'svg' in allowedAssetTypes, lines 596-598 performed only extension allowlisting, and line 603 moved the uploaded file into the theme assets path without parsing or sanitizing SVG content. This combination, not later handler renames, formatting, or the 2016 move to shared file definitions, is the smallest public-history commit that wrote the vulnerable mechanism.
ai_marker: absent — the exact commit object for 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 records author and committer as Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com> and message 'Welcome to the world, October :-)'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot-author, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-m7gw-rffq-rxjm (also returned by https://api.github.com/repos/wintercms/winter/security-advisories/GHSA-m7gw-rffq-rxjm) identifies CVE-2026-22254, winter/wn-cms-module <=1.2.9, patched version 1.2.10, the cms.manage_assets prerequisite, unsanitized SVG uploads, and fix https://github.com/wintercms/winter/commit/8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65.

At v1.2.9 (tag commit eb88fed4c13abaf826cf4929c69897cdd8262fc1), modules/cms/controllers/Index.php:49-55 includes cms.manage_assets in the CMS controller permission gate. modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php:623-631 lowercases and allowlists only the filename extension, lines 640-684 accept file_data and move it unchanged into getCurrentPath(), and lines 434-441 map that destination to the theme's /assets directory and a themes/<theme>/assets URL.

Vulnerability-first history: git log -L over onUpload/checkUploadPostback and git log --all --reverse --follow -S '$uploadedFile->move($this->getCurrentPath()' -- modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php both lead to 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5. git log -S "'svg'" shows the same commit as the earliest write of the SVG allowance. The commit's modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php:56 allows svg and lines 574-603 validate size/extension then move raw bytes.

Direct-parent proof: git cat-file -p 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 gives the sole parent d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827. git cat-file -e d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827:modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php fails because the path is absent, while git diff d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 -- modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php shows the file, SVG allowlist, and raw upload move created from /dev/null. Thus the vulnerable lines are absent in the immediate parent tree.

Commit-object-only AI check: git cat-file -p 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 shows author Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>, committer Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>, one parent, and only the message 'Welcome to the world, October :-)'. There are no AI identities or attribution trailers. No later commit, PR text, or fix authorship was used for the AI verdict.

Fix evidence: the direct patch 8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65 modifies modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php so that, after extension validation and before move(), an svg upload is rewritten through Svg::extract(), and the destination uses the validated filename. The advisory points directly to this non-merge commit, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are identical.

Release-boundary proof: v1.2.9 resolves to eb88fed4c13abaf826cf4929c69897cdd8262fc1 and contains 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 but not 8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65; v1.2.10 resolves to 9e456ee96227b26763b9a8e00554f238614aea56 and contains both. The v1.2.10 tree at modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php:687-694 contains the Svg::extract() rewrite before move(). The earliest extant v1 tag, v1.0.319 (ca3e13ed330d97fab89c75cfb826a006d126ce67), also contains the BIC and raw move, so the BIC predates the affected Winter release line. First-party release URL: https://github.com/wintercms/winter/releases/tag/v1.2.10.

Lifecycle follow-up: 18c98abc85219fac5cdac80161b45160dbdd55d0 (first contained by v1.2.11) later lowercased the SVG extension check and sanitized files renamed to an SVG extension. That hardening does not change which commit first wrote the vulnerable raw-upload mechanism or the advisory's cited 8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65 / v1.2.10 boundary.
reasoning: The advisory's mechanism is borne out by the affected source: a permission-gated backend upload reaches AssetList::onUpload, where SVG is an accepted asset type and the file is persisted under a public theme-assets URL without content sanitization. Line history distinguishes the origin from later changes: 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 simultaneously created the SVG allowance and raw move; subsequent commits merely refactored validation, permissions, and handler shape until 8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65 inserted sanitization. Its sole direct parent d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827 has no AssetList.php path, proving parent absence. Tag ancestry matches the declared boundary: the BIC is in affected releases through v1.2.9, the cited fix is absent from v1.2.9, and both the fix commit and sanitization lines are present in v1.2.10. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent repository commit with no member-commit chain to decompose. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI marker or attribution trailer, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any later history.
